entries.name: fs.readFile()
entries.description: Asynchronously reads the entire contents of a file. Returns a Buffer by default, or a string when encoding is specified.
entries.syntax:
fs.readFile(path, callback)
fs.readFile(path, options, callback)

// Promise version (recommended)
await fs.promises.readFile(path, options)

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: (err, data) callback. Use promises API instead when possible.

examples.title: Read file as string (async/await)
Read binary file
Callback style

bestPractices: Use fs/promises (async/await) rather than callback style
Always specify encoding for text files to get a string instead of Buffer

entries.name: fs.writeFile()
entries.description: Asynchronously writes data to a file, replacing the file if it already exists. Creates the file if it doesn't exist.

examples.title: Write text to file
Append to file
examples.code:
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

await writeFile('./log.txt', `${new Date().toISOString()} - Event\n`, { flag: 'a', encoding: 'utf-8' });

commonMistakes: Not creating parent directories first — use mkdir with recursive:true
bestPractices: Use { flag: 'a' } to append instead of overwrite

entries.name: fs.readdir()
entries.description: Reads the contents of a directory, returning an array of file names. Use withFileTypes: true to get Dirent objects with isFile/isDirectory methods.

examples.title: List files in directory
List with types
Recursive listing (Node 18.17+)
examples.code:
const allFiles = await readdir('./src', { recursive: true });
console.log(allFiles);

entries.name: fs.mkdir()
entries.description: Asynchronously creates a directory. Use recursive: true to create nested directories without errors if they already exist.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path of the directory to create.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Options. Use recursive: true to create nested dirs.

examples.title: Create nested directories

bestPractices: Always use recursive: true unless you specifically need to detect existing dirs

entries.name: fs.stat()
entries.description: Returns information about a file or directory (size, modification time, type). Use .isFile(), .isDirectory() to check entry type.

examples.title: Check file size and type
Safe file exists check

entries.name: fs.createReadStream()
entries.description: Creates a readable stream for a file. Efficient for large files as it reads in chunks rather than loading the whole file into memory.

examples.title: Pipe file to HTTP response
Process CSV line by line

entries.name: path.join()
entries.description: Joins path segments together using the platform-specific separator, normalizing the result.

examples.title: Join path parts
Build path from __dirname

commonMistakes: Hardcoding / or \ separators instead of using path.join — breaks cross-platform
bestPractices: Always use path.join() or path.resolve() for cross-platform path construction

entries.name: path.resolve()
entries.description: Resolves a sequence of paths into an absolute path, processing from right to left until an absolute path is constructed.

examples.title: Resolve absolute path

entries.name: path.dirname()
entries.description: Returns the directory name of a path, similar to the Unix dirname command.

examples.title: Get parent directory
ESM __dirname equivalent

entries.name: path.basename()
entries.description: Returns the last portion of a path (the filename), optionally removing the extension.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional extension to remove from the result.

examples.title: Get filename
examples.code:
import path from 'node:path';

console.log(path.basename('/usr/local/bin/node')); // 'node'
console.log(path.basename('./src/index.ts'));       // 'index.ts'
console.log(path.basename('./src/index.ts', '.ts')); // 'index'

entries.name: path.extname()
entries.description: Returns the file extension of a path, from the last occurrence of . to the end of the string.

examples.title: Get extension
examples.code:
import path from 'node:path';

console.log(path.extname('index.html')); // '.html'
console.log(path.extname('archive.tar.gz')); // '.gz'
console.log(path.extname('no-extension')); // ''

entries.name: crypto.createHash()
entries.description: Creates and returns a Hash object that can be used to generate fixed-size digests from data. Common algorithms: 'sha256', 'sha512', 'md5'.

examples.title: SHA-256 hash
Hash a file

commonMistakes: Using MD5 for security — it is cryptographically broken. Use SHA-256 or higher.
bestPractices: Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for checksums

entries.name: crypto.createHmac()
entries.description: Creates and returns an Hmac object — a keyed hash for message authentication. Used for API signatures and webhook verification.

examples.title: Sign a message
Verify webhook signature

entries.name: crypto.randomBytes()
entries.description: Generates cryptographically strong pseudo-random bytes. Use for tokens, salts, IDs, and secrets.

examples.title: Generate secure token
Generate UUID v4 equivalent
examples.code:
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

const id = randomUUID(); // 'b3b14a25-5619-4b48-b5fb-ef1234567890'

entries.name: process.env
entries.description: An object containing the user environment variables. Used to configure applications without hardcoding sensitive data like API keys, database URLs, and feature flags.

examples.title: Access environment variables
Feature flags

bestPractices: Use a .env file with dotenv for local development
Validate required env vars at startup
Never commit secrets to version control

entries.name: process.exit()
entries.description: Terminates the Node.js process with the specified exit code. Exit code 0 means success; non-zero means an error occurred.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Exit code. 0 = success, non-zero = error. Defaults to 0.

examples.title: Exit on fatal error
CLI tool exit codes

entries.name: process.argv
entries.description: An array containing the command-line arguments. argv[0] is 'node', argv[1] is the script path, and argv[2+] are user arguments.

examples.title: Parse CLI arguments

entries.name: process.cwd()
entries.description: Returns the current working directory of the Node.js process as a string.

examples.title: Get working directory

entries.name: process.nextTick()
entries.description: Schedules a callback to be called at the end of the current event loop iteration (before I/O events and timers). Higher priority than setImmediate and setTimeout.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Arguments to pass to the callback.

examples.title: Defer to next tick

entries.name: http.createServer()
entries.description: Creates a new HTTP server. The request handler receives IncomingMessage (req) and ServerResponse (res) objects.
entries.syntax:
http.createServer(requestListener)
http.createServer(options, requestListener)

requestListener(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse)

parameters.name: requestListener
parameters.description: Function called for each request with (req, res).

examples.title: Basic HTTP server

entries.complexity: O(1) to create; O(1) per request

entries.name: EventEmitter
entries.description: The core event system in Node.js. Classes can extend EventEmitter to emit and listen to named events.

examples.title: Basic event emitter
Extend EventEmitter

entries.name: child_process.exec()
entries.description: Spawns a shell to run a command. Use for short-lived commands where you need the full output. For large outputs or streaming, use spawn().

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command to run in a shell.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Options including cwd, env, timeout, maxBuffer.

examples.title: Run shell command
List files
examples.code:
const { stdout } = await execAsync('ls -la', { cwd: '/usr/local' });
console.log(stdout);

commonMistakes: Using exec with unsanitized user input — shell injection risk! Use spawn() instead
bestPractices: Use spawn() when you need to pass user input safely
Set maxBuffer option for large outputs

entries.name: child_process.spawn()
entries.description: Spawns a new process with the given command. Does NOT use a shell by default, making it safe for user-provided arguments. Streams output.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: List of arguments. Each argument is passed safely — no shell injection.

examples.title: Safe command with user args

entries.name: stream.pipeline()
entries.description: Pipes streams together and handles errors and cleanup automatically. The recommended way to work with Node.js streams — it destroys all streams on error.
entries.syntax:
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';
await pipeline(source, ...transforms, destination)

parameters.name: streams
parameters.description: Source, optional transform streams, and destination.

examples.title: Compress a file
Fetch and save

entries.name: Buffer.from()
entries.description: Creates a new Buffer from a string, array, ArrayBuffer, or another Buffer. Used for binary data manipulation.
entries.syntax:
Buffer.from(string, encoding?)
Buffer.from(array)
Buffer.from(arrayBuffer, byteOffset?, length?)
Buffer.from(buffer)

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: String to encode into a Buffer.

examples.title: Encode string
examples.code:
const buf = Buffer.from('Hello, World!', 'utf-8');
console.log(buf);               // <Buffer 48 65 6c 6c 6f ...>
console.log(buf.toString());    // 'Hello, World!'
console.log(buf.toString('hex')); // '48656c6c6f...'

examples.title: Base64 encode/decode

entries.name: Buffer.alloc()
entries.description: Allocates a new Buffer of specified size, filled with zeros by default. Safe alternative to Buffer.allocUnsafe().
entries.syntax:
Buffer.alloc(size)
Buffer.alloc(size, fill)
Buffer.alloc(size, fill, encoding)

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Length of the Buffer in bytes.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Value to fill the Buffer with. Defaults to 0.

examples.title: Allocate zeroed buffer
examples.code:
const buf = Buffer.alloc(10); // 10 bytes, all zeros
console.log(buf); // <Buffer 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00>

examples.title: Allocate filled buffer
examples.code:
const buf = Buffer.alloc(5, 'A');
console.log(buf.toString()); // 'AAAAA'

entries.name: setTimeout()
entries.description: Schedules a function to be called after a minimum delay (in milliseconds). Returns a Timeout handle that can be used to cancel with clearTimeout().

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: The function to execute after the delay.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: Milliseconds to wait before calling callback.

examples.title: Delay execution
Promise-based delay
Cancel timeout
examples.code:
const timer = setTimeout(() => console.log('This will not run'), 5000);
clearTimeout(timer); // Cancelled before it fires

entries.name: setInterval()
entries.description: Schedules a function to be repeatedly called with a fixed delay between each call. Returns an Interval handle.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: Function to call on each interval.

examples.title: Polling example
